title: How to Protect Your Indie Games from AI
author: guilemo

comments.author: i_rate_slop
comments.body:
Because my brain is fried by TikTok and AI, I needed this condensed:

\- Build a distinctive game. A strong story and interacting mechanics require more work to copy than one simple mechanic.

\- Keep complexity purposeful. Extra complexity increases development work. Add features because they improve the game.

\- Include only necessary content in demos. Remove code and assets for unreleased features. Disabled features remain in the distributed files. Someone could extract them or remove the restrictions.

\- Start with trusted testers. Small groups reduce exposure. However, they can provide less varied feedback than public tests.

\- Give test builds unique identifiers. These identifiers can help trace a leaked build. They do not prevent leaks.

\- Limit work on encryption. It might delay copying near launch. It does not guarantee lasting protection.

\- Report copying to platform operators. Reports help operators identify problems and can support demands for better protection.

\- Continue to improve your skills. AI tools do not automatically provide design judgment, artistic direction, or a coherent game.

\- Treat these measures as risk reduction. They can limit exposure and increase the effort needed to copy your game. They cannot prevent all copying.

replies.author: yaxir
replies.body:
There is a big fucking reason why humans are called idiots and stupid. I'm not calling you any of these. I'm talking about the general employment market. I think corporate greed, capitalist greed, and a lot of this numbnut nonsense have caused people to make really stupid decisions.

I don't think graphic designers and animators are obsolete. They will just need to repurpose themselves. Believe me, man, I'm a highly technical guy and I'm trying to make a game that I really would like to play and really would like to share with the world. I'm almost thinking about giving up because I can't do the animation. I don't know about all those keys, frames, and ticks because that is a part I never touched. I'm more of an engineering person. You can even say I'm more of a scientist than someone who deals with the graphics side of things.

I would love it if I had a childhood friend or friends, or someone who was a badass animator, because then we would make a great team. He or she would do the animations and design the assets and I would take care of the coding side and the logic side of the thing.

You see the only fucking shit is that it is so hard right now. You need to understand: I think society is blowing this out of proportion, as they always do. Artists, graphic artists, all these people, they are not necessarily useless. I think it's kind of jumping to a conclusion if you say, "Oh you are useless because a tool came out called AI and it can just do stuff that you can do." I think their roles will change somehow. They might have to learn new crafts but that's about it.

Right now I don't know what to tell you. I'm trying so much to get some sort of automated framework going and I think I also made a post about assets on a few subs on Reddit. Even though I'm getting some great advice, I don't think I will have the time to do all that because I got other shit to do in life. I disagree with you. These animators, these artists, they just need to repurpose themselves. They'll be just fine.

comments.author: monchikun
comments.body:
I'll ad another important element and that is networking. Connections within the game industry particularly with publishers and biz dev teams. Connect with communities and influencers. The more of a human moat you build around your game the more chances you give your project. I assume that kost copycats rely on just releasing to see what sticks but in the era of near-infinite content these attempts will typically drop of because they will likely not have any kind of marketing support (organic or paid). 

With more and more games being released developers must start thinking like marketers and community managers.
